tools.name: get_challenge
tools.description: Step 1 of writing to Caper: a single-use ROLA challenge (5-minute expiry). The response includes the exact recipe for the message your Ed25519 key must sign. Writes are Stokenet-testnet only for now, and you always sign with your OWN key – nothing here custodies anything. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Step 2: exchange the signed ROLA proof for a 12h Bearer token – the same verification the human wallet flow runs. Send the returned token as an HTTP `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on every later tool call; MCP arguments never carry it.

tools.name: get_manifest
tools.description: Step 3: a ready-to-sign transaction manifest. Kinds: create-caper, buy, sell, create-proposal. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_wiki, get_recent_changes, list_daos, get_challenge, get_manifest, submit_tx · Private data: get_full_corpus, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page · Public sink: list_daos, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_wiki, get_recent_changes, list_daos, get_challenge, get_manifest, submit_tx · Private data: get_full_corpus, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page · Public sink: list_daos, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
